message.content: The exact count of mitochondria varies widely among cell types and even within the same cell type under different conditions. In most mammalian cells you’ll find somewhere between **50 and 500 mitochondria** per cell. Cells with high energy demands—such as skeletal muscle fibers, cardiac myocytes, or neurons—can contain thousands of mitochondria, whereas other cell types may have fewer. The number also fluctuates during the cell cycle and in response to metabolic cues.
